question: An 80-year-old lady who has been admitted to the hospital with confusion and become agitated. She has pulled off her intravenous cannula and she is shouting and hitting the medical staff.
explanation: Delirium in elderly requires haloperidol, lowest possible dose.

question: A 25 year-old with schizophrenia has been treated with the first-line medication of atypical antipsychotics but she has not responded.
explanation: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia requires clozapine.

question: A 9-year-old boy has had a headache for the past 5 months. He describes the headache as throbbing in nature. Every time he comes home from school he goes straight to sleep. The headaches are affecting his performance at school.
explanation: Throbbing headache affecting school indicates migraine.

question: A 30-year-old woman presents to the emergency with a sudden onset of headache as if she has been hit at the back of her head.
explanation: Sudden onset occipital headache suggests subarachnoid hemorrhage.

question: A 45-year-old man presents with unilateral headache and left eye pain. On examination he has an injection of the left eye.
explanation: Unilateral headache with eye pain and redness suggests cluster headache.

question: A 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with hypertension presents with erectile dysfunction.
explanation: Beta-blockers like bisoprolol commonly cause erectile dysfunction.

question: A 23-year-old man who is in a new relationship fails to sustain an erection. He has early morning erections.
explanation: New relationship stress with preserved morning erections indicates psychogenic cause.

question: A 46-year-old man presents with a history of loss of interest in daily activities, poor sleep and early morning awakening. He recently visited his general practitioner for treatment of his symptoms.
explanation: SSRIs like citalopram can cause erectile dysfunction.

question: A 30-year-old woman who is 24 weeks pregnant is found to have a blood pressure of 140/90 and protein++ on urine dipstick.
explanation: Mild pre-eclampsia (140/90) requires monitoring, not medication. NB- NICE GUIDELINES SAY START TREATMENT

question: A 30-year-old woman who is 10 weeks pregnant has a blood pressure of 138/83. She has a history of pre-eclampsia in pregnancy.
explanation: Normal BP at 10 weeks, too early for gestational hypertension diagnosis.

question: A 4-year-old child is brought to the general practitioner with constipation.
explanation: Macrogol is first-line for pediatric constipation.

question: A 6-month-old child vomits every food he is fed but he is gaining weight properly.
explanation: Gastroesophageal reflux disease responds to H2 antagonist cimetidine.

question: An 83-year-old lady presents with visual problems. She can see the edges of the clock but can not read the time.
explanation: Central vision loss with preserved periphery indicates macular degeneration.

question: A 55-year-old man presents because he sees dark specs in his vision which moves around his vision when he moves his eye from left to right. It gets better when he wears glasses.
explanation: Moving dark specs suggest vitreous hemorrhage.

question: An 83-year-old man presents with a gradual loss of vision. He experiences glare at night especially when driving. He has realized that his symptoms are worse when the headlight flashes at him. This has stopped him from driving at night.
explanation: Glare at night and gradual vision loss indicate cataract.

question: A 2-year-old girl presents with fever and limping. On examination her right knee is swollen.
explanation: Fever, swollen knee in child indicates septic arthritis.

question: A 14-year-old boy presents with limping and hip pain. The pain is worse when he sits too long.
explanation: Teenager with hip pain worse on sitting suggests slipped epiphysis.

question: A 7-year-old boy has had abdominal pain and diarrhoea for 4 months. He has weight loss and anaemia.
explanation: Chronic diarrhea, weight loss, anemia suggest coeliac disease.

question: A 10-year-old boy presents with bloody diarrhoea. He has a purpuric rash on his abdomen, buttocks and abdominal pain.
explanation: Bloody diarrhea with purpuric rash suggests HSP vasculitis.

question: A two-year-old boy has had bloody diarrhoea and vomiting for the last 2 days. When he cries he pulls his leg towards his abdomen.
explanation: Bloody stool, vomiting, leg pulling suggest intussusception.

question: A 70-year-old man presents with back pain. The straight leg raise test is 40 degrees on both legs. He has a pulsatile abdominal mass.
explanation: Pulsatile abdominal mass indicates AAA requiring urgent admission.

question: A 28-year-old woman presents with localized lower back pain. She has been given analgesia and his pain is well controlled.
explanation: Controlled back pain should be mobilized to prevent deconditioning.

question: A 19-year-old girl presents with 2 days history of back pain. She is noticed to be dragging her leg.
explanation: Acute back pain with leg dragging suggests nerve compression requiring urgent admission. NB- BOTH OPTIONS E AND I ARE SAME

question: A 66-year-old man who has a long-standing smoking history is brought by the wife with loss of appetite and weakness. Blood tests show Hb 11, Na+ 128.
explanation: Smoker with hyponatremia suggests small cell lung cancer with SIADH.

question: An 83-year-old lady is brought to the hospital by her daughter with immobility and confusion. She was recently diagnosed with depression. Blood tests show low sodium.
explanation: SSRIs like citalopram can cause hyponatremia and confusion.

question: A 24-year-old lady presents with weight loss and tremors in the arms. TSH 0.3, T4 32.
explanation: Low TSH with high T4 indicates hyperthyroidism.

question: A 25-year-old lady presents with weight gain. TSH 6.3, T4 5.
explanation: High TSH with low T4 indicates hypothyroidism.

question: A man presents feeling unwell. TSH 0.3, T4 3.2.
explanation: Low TSH and low T4 in ill patient indicates sick euthyroid syndrome.

question: A 4-month-old baby is brought to the paediatric department with fever, shortness of breath and poor feeding. On examination, he has got bilateral wheeze.
explanation: RSV is the most common cause of bronchiolitis in infants.

question: A 6-month-old child is brought with bouts of coughing which ends with a retch.
explanation: Whooping cough causes bouts ending with retch.

question: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the hospital with a barking cough.
explanation: Parainfluenza virus causes croup with barking cough.

question: A 12-month-old child has a fever of 39°Celsius. She is sitting on her mother's lap unable to swallow saliva.
explanation: High fever with inability to swallow saliva indicates epiglottitis caused by H. influenzae.

question: A 4-month-old girl is brought by her mother with fever, cough, difficulty in breathing and shortness of breath. Oxygen saturation is 92% on air and she has bilateral wheeze.
explanation: Infant with fever, wheeze, desaturation indicates bronchiolitis.

question: A 4-year-old child is brought with fever and cough. He is noticed to have bouts of cough which end with a retch.
explanation: Bouts of cough ending with retch indicate whooping cough.

question: A 3-year-old boy is brought with a cough. On examination he has a wheeze on the right upper zone which is monophasic.
explanation: Monophasic localized wheeze suggests foreign body aspiration.

question: A 10-year-old child presents with mild colicky abdominal pain. He has had 4 episodes of diarrhoea in the past 24 hours. Temperature: 36.8 degrees Celsius.
explanation: Mild diarrhea with normal temperature requires no antibiotics.

question: A 30-year-old man presents with a 5-day history of ear pain.
explanation: Acute otitis media >3 days requires amoxicillin.

question: A 56-year-old man has had worsening of frequency of micturition and dysuria in the last 2 days.
explanation: Frequency with dysuria indicates UTI requiring antibiotics.

question: A 64-year-old man presents with frequency in micturition, nocturia and dribbling. On examination he has an enlarged smooth prostate gland with a deep median sulcus.
explanation: BPH symptoms require alpha-blockers as first-line treatment.

question: A 61-year-old woman has had urinary incontinence with an urge to pass urine. She has had two months of bladder training with no improvement.
explanation: Failed bladder training requires antimuscarinic for urge incontinence.

question: A 28-year-old lady presents with numbness in her thumb and first three fingers. She has got no wasting of the muscles. What is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome: night splinting first-line.

question: A 41-year-old man has got burning and numbness in the first, second, third and fourth fingers. What is the most appropriate investigation?
explanation: Nerve conduction studies confirm carpal tunnel syndrome.

question: A 30-year-old lady presents with a dry cough. She has a rash on her leg which has got a pale central area. Chest X-ray shows bilateral patchy consolidation.
explanation: Bilateral patchy consolidation with erythema multiforme suggests mycoplasma.

question: A 32-year-old man sustained a contusion to the chest yesterday while playing football. He has presented with chest pain. On examination the chest is clear but he has a bruise and tenderness on the left side over the third and fourth ribs.
explanation: Musculoskeletal chest pain from contusion requires NSAIDs.

question: A 37-year-old man presents with day time tiredness. In the evening after every meal he gets sleepy straight away.
explanation: Daytime somnolence requires Epworth Sleepiness Scale assessment.

question: A 21-year-old man drinks a lot of water and passes urine more frequently. He has a reddish scaly nodule on his shin.
explanation: Polyuria, polydipsia with necrobiosis lipoidica indicates diabetes.

question: A 65-year-old lady presents with pain on her face. The pain is triggered by chewing or touching the face. What is the most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Trigeminal neuralgia requires carbamazepine first-line.

question: A 28-year-old man with past history of hay fever presents with shortness of breath on exercise. He has had wheeze in the past while at the farm. On examination he has bilateral crackles but his chest X-ray is normal.
explanation: Farm exposure with bilateral crackles suggests allergic alveolitis.

question: A 23-year-old man presents with shortness of breath on exertion, bilateral lower limb oedema and myopia.
explanation: Young with heart failure and myopia suggests Marfan's syndrome.

question: A 10-year-old boy presents with abdominal pain. He recently had a sore throat, cough and running nose. His temperature is 36.7 degrees celsius and his abdominal examination is normal.
explanation: Normal exam and temperature after viral illness suggests constipation. normal exam and no fever excludes mesenteric adenitis.

question: An 83-year-old lady presents to the general practitioner with acute onset of weakness of the left arm and speech disturbance for two hours.
explanation: Acute stroke symptoms require immediate hospital admission.

question: A 28-year-old lady presents with right leg weakness for the past 3 days. 2 years ago, she had an acute loss of vision in the left eye which resolved after 3 weeks.
explanation: Multiple sclerosis investigation requires MRI brain.

question: A 25-year-old man with paranoid delusion and derogatory hallucinations was given haloperidol. Shortly afterwards he develops high blood pressure, tachycardia and muscle rigidity.
explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome causes elevated CK.

question: A 29-year-old woman has had 3 consecutive miscarriages. She has a past history of two episodes of deep venous thromboembolism.
explanation: Recurrent miscarriage with DVT history suggests thrombophilia.

question: A 17-year-old boy has had recurrent nosebleed. He is found to have iron deficiency anemia but a normal platelet count.
explanation: Recurrent nosebleeds with iron deficiency suggest HHT.

question: A 19-year-old man has had abdominal pains. His cousin died of a brain haemorrhage. Abdominal examination is normal and urine dipstick shows blood++ and protein++.
explanation: Family history of brain hemorrhage with hematuria indicates PKD.

question: A 32-year-old woman has had upper abdominal pain and reflux.
explanation: Upper abdominal pain with reflux needs ultrasound for gallstones.

question: A 15-year-old boy is brought to the general practitioner by his mother with gynecomastia. On examination he has small testes, failure of erection and low testosterone levels.
explanation: Gynecomastia, small testes, low testosterone indicate Klinefelter's.

question: A 60-year-old man with a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus and Addison's disease has not taken his medication for the last 3 days. He presents with confusion, fatigue and tiredness.
explanation: Sudden steroid withdrawal causes adrenal crisis.

question: A 23-year-old man presents with penile ulcer. When he gets an erection, he experiences severe pain. On examination, he has a whitish shiny lesion and an ulcer on his foreskin.
explanation: White shiny lesion with painful erection suggests lichen sclerosis.

question: A 30-year-old woman who is 29 weeks pregnant presents with lower abdominal pain, dysuria and frequency of micturition. Urine dipstick shows nitrites ++ and leucocytes +.
explanation: Pregnancy UTI requires cefalexin (trimethoprim contraindicated).

question: An 83-year-old lady presents with abdominal pain and rectal bleed. She has got a history of oesophagitis.
explanation: Elderly with rectal bleeding suggests colon cancer.

question: A 60-year-old man presents with abdominal pain. A computerised tomography scan shows an abdominal aortic aneurysm which is 7cm in size. He has a history of hypertension.
explanation: 7cm AAA requires urgent hospital admission.

question: An 83-year-old lady presents with pigmented itchy rash on the lower legs. The pigmentation had appeared before. On examination, she has got a nodule on the shin which is oval and about 2 cm in diameter.
explanation: Elderly with round nodules on shin indicates discoid eczema.

question: A 17-year-old woman presents with abdominal pain. Her last menstrual period was 6 weeks ago. She has left iliac fossa tenderness.
explanation: Abdominal pain with LMP 6 weeks ago needs pregnancy test first.

question: A 56-year-old lady presents with multiple vulvar lesions which are pedunculated and painless.
explanation: Pedunculated painless vulvar lesions are genital warts.

question: A 5-year-old boy presents with a blistering rash around the mouth, face and nose. On examination, he has got a golden brown, honey-coloured crusted lesion. What is the most appropriate management?
explanation: Impetigo requires flucloxacillin.

question: An 18-year-old lady with a history of asthma presents with an itchy rash all over her body. What is the most likely aetiology?
explanation: Asthma history with itchy rash indicates atopic dermatitis.

question: A 65-year-old woman passes urine every time she laughs. She was recently put on treatment. She complains of dry mouth. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Stress incontinence treated with duloxetine causes dry mouth.

question: A 75-year-old man with prostate cancer develops back pain and weakness in both legs. He has perianal paraesthesia. What is the IMMEDIATE management?
explanation: Spinal cord compression requires immediate dexamethasone.

question: A 12-year-old girl with a history of asthma was exposed to pollen. She presents with shortness of breath, rash and wheeze. What is the SINGLE most important medication to give?
explanation: Anaphylaxis requires immediate intramuscular adrenaline.

question: A 19-year-old footballer complains of dizziness while training.
explanation: Young athlete with dizziness suggests hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

question: A 46-year-old man who is obese sleeps in a different room from his wife because he snores a lot at night. He has constipation and erectile dysfunction.
explanation: Obesity with snoring, constipation, ED suggests hypothyroidism.

question: A 70-year-old man who is known to have bronchiectasis presents with productive cough with greenish sputum for the last one week.
explanation: Chest infection in bronchiectasis needs chest X-ray.

question: A 24-year-old boy presents with scaly lesions on both legs.
explanation: Scaly leg lesions require emollients for eczema or psoriasis.

question: A 75-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer 5 years ago presents with chest pain. On examination, she has tenderness on the right side of her chest. Blood tests show hypercalcemia.
explanation: Breast cancer history with hypercalcemia indicates bone metastases.

question: Which of the following causes water retention in the kidneys?
explanation: Vasopressin (ADH) causes water reabsorption in kidneys. it acts on the distal tubules and collecting ducts

question: A 26-year-old man who smokes 20 cigarettes a day presents with chest pain radiating to the neck.
explanation: Young smoker with chest pain radiating to neck suggests GORD.

question: A 36-year-old woman presents with dry cough for the last one month. She has red eyes and nodules on her shin.
explanation: Dry cough, red eyes, erythema nodosum indicate sarcoidosis.

question: A 59-year-old lady with type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with burning pain in both legs.
explanation: Diabetic neuropathy pain treated with gabapentin.

question: A 62-year-old man has pain in his right big toe for which he has been taking diclofenac and ibuprofen. He has presented with reduced urine output.
explanation: NSAID use causing reduced urine output suggests interstitial nephritis.

question: A 19-year-old boy presents with tiredness. He has noticed that his gums bleed easily while brushing his teeth.
explanation: Gum bleeding with tiredness in young patient suggests leukemia.

question: An 83-year-old lady presents with chronic back pain. Blood tests show anaemia, high ESR, high creatinine, hypercalcemia.
explanation: Back pain with anemia, high ESR, renal failure, hypercalcemia indicates myeloma.

question: A 55-year-old man is found to have blood++ in the urine on a dipstick. He does not have any symptoms.
explanation: Painless hematuria suggests bladder cancer.

question: A 55-year-old man presents with ataxia and confusion. He is noticed to be using big words and making up stories.
explanation: Confabulation with ataxia indicates Wernicke-Korsakoff from B1 deficiency.

question: A 29-year-old man presents with loin to groin pain.
explanation: Renal colic pain best treated with IM diclofenac.

question: A 25-year-old, first time mother attend with a 2-year-old boy with complaints of a child developing rash and diarrhoea after feeding.
explanation: Rash and diarrhea after feeding suggests cow's milk allergy.

question: A 36-year-old woman with heavy menstrual periods need contraception.
explanation: Mirena is first-line for menorrhagia and long-term contraception.

question: A 37-year-old woman who completed her family wants contraception. She is a heavy smoker.
explanation: IUCD is best for smokers who've completed family - no hormones, long-term, safe with smoking.

question: A 58-year-old man with hypertension developed swelling of the ankle.
explanation: Calcium channel blockers like amlodipine cause ankle swelling as vasodilatory side effect.

question: A 45-year-old man with hypertension, myocardial infarction and diabetes, develops angioedema.
explanation: ACE inhibitors like lisinopril commonly cause angioedema due to bradykinin accumulation.

question: A 19-year-old boy presents with sudden onset of shortness of breath which started the previous day while playing football.
explanation: Sudden SOB in tall young male during exercise is classic for pneumothorax.

question: A 30-year-old woman who is on combined oral contraceptive pill developed sudden chest pain and shortness of breath 2 days ago. She arrived from Australia 5 days ago.
explanation: SOB and chest pain in young woman on COCP with recent long flight suggests PE.

question: A 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension presents with central chest pain that radiates to the back
explanation: Chest pain radiating to back in hypertensive patient is aortic dissection until proven otherwise.

question: A 22-year-old man presents with acute chest pain relieved by leaning forward. He has a temperature of 37.8 degrees Celsius. He had a flu-like illness 10 days ago.

options.a: Tachycardia and T-wave inversion V1 to V3
options.b: ST elevation in lead II, III and aVF
options.d: ST depression in lead II, III and aVF
options.g: T wave inversion and Q wave

explanation: Pericarditis presents with widespread saddle-shaped ST elevation. Chest pain relieved by leaning forward is classic.

question: A 56-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes type 2 presents with central crushing chest pain which radiates to the left arm. His temperature is 36.7 degrees Celsius and he has sweaty palms.

options.a: Tachycardia and T-wave inversion V1 to V3
options.b: ST elevation in lead II, III and aVF
options.d: ST depression in lead II, III and aVF
options.g: T wave inversion and Q wave

explanation: MI presents with ST elevation. Hypertension and diabetes are risk factors. Typical cardiac pain and sweating support diagnosis.

question: A 32-year-old man who has been admitted with an exacerbation of asthma is found to have a potassium of 7.2mmol/L

options.a: Tachycardia and T-wave inversion V1 to V3
options.b: ST elevation in lead II, III and aVF
options.d: ST depression in lead II, III and aVF
options.g: T wave inversion and Q wave

explanation: Hyperkalemia causes tall peaked T-waves on ECG. Potassium of 7.2 is life-threatening hyperkalemia.

question: A 62-year-old man was started on simvastatin 2 months ago. He complains of muscle aches.
explanation: Simvastatin can cause rhabdomyolysis. CK is the key investigation for muscle breakdown.

question: A 53-year-old man who was started on clindamycin for cellulitis developed diarrhoea for 5 days. The diarrhoea has resolved but the patient has now developed confusion and fatigue.
explanation: Recent diarrhea can cause hyponatraemia leading to confusion and fatigue. U&E assesses electrolytes.

question: A 45-year-old man who was started on lithium for bipolar disorder develops tremors in his hands. Lithium levels, urea and electrolytes are all normal.
explanation: Lithium can cause hyperthyroidism. Tremors with normal lithium levels suggest thyroid dysfunction.

question: A 56-year-old man with diabetes mellitus type 2 is found to have hypoalbuminemia and his blood pressure reading is 130/80mmHg.
explanation: Diabetic nephropathy with hypoalbuminemia requires ACE inhibitor (lisinopril) to reduce mortality.

question: A 57-year-old man with a long-standing history of diabetes type 1 presents with vision loss. On fundoscopy examination there is formation of new vessels.
explanation: New vessel formation indicates proliferative diabetic retinopathy requiring laser photocoagulation.

question: A 40-year-old man with a long-standing diabetes type 2 presents with a burning sensation in the legs.
explanation: Burning sensation suggests diabetic neuropathy. Gabapentin is first-line for neuropathic pain.

question: A 39-year-old man presents with upper arm weakness. On examination, you notice that he has multiple burns to his fingers. When asked about it, he says he feels no pains in his fingers.
explanation: Loss of pain sensation with preserved touch suggests syringomyelia affecting spinothalamic tract.

question: A 45-year-old man is referred to the neurology clinic because he has been dropping objects from his hands. He has also noticed that his hand grip has become weak. On examination, he has muscle wasting and fasciculations in both upper arms.
explanation: Muscle weakness, wasting and fasciculations are signs of lower motor neuron lesion in MND.

question: An 18-year-old girl presents with weakness in her right arm. 3 months ago she had lost vision in the left eye which resolved after 2 weeks.
explanation: Relapsing-remitting pattern with optic neuritis and arm weakness suggests multiple sclerosis.

question: A 4-year-old child is brought with a red rash on the body. On examination, the rash looks like small grains. The child's tongue is also noted to be red.
explanation: Sandpaper-like rash with strawberry tongue is classic for scarlet fever caused by Streptococcus.

question: A 7-year-old boy is found to have rash on his hands and feet. He has had a fever for 5 days. On examination he has cervical lymphadenopathy and a red tongue.
explanation: Fever >5 days, rash on hands/feet, cervical lymphadenopathy and strawberry tongue are Kawasaki criteria.

question: A 6-month-old child is brought to the emergency department with fever and rash on his face. On examination, he has a rash on both cheeks and peri-oral area.
explanation: Slapped cheek rash in young child with fever is characteristic of parvovirus B19 infection.

question: A 19-year-old woman had unprotected sexual intercourse 48 hours ago. She is in a stable relationship.
explanation: note that iucd  is the best in absence of contraindications. Levonorgestrel is emergency contraception effective up to 72 hours after unprotected intercourse.

question: A 32-year-old woman with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease and hypertension requests contraception advice.
explanation: History of PID contraindicates IUCD. Hypertension contraindicates combined pills. POP is safest option.

question: A 30-year-old lady who is 20 days postpartum is requesting contraception. She had a caesarian section.
explanation: Postpartum <21 days, progesterone only pill is suitable. No indication for long-term methods.

question: A 57-year-old man presents with fever, shortness of breath and cough with greenish sputum.
explanation: Community-acquired pneumonia first-line treatment is oral amoxicillin for mild to moderate infection.

question: A 62-year-old man presents with a burning sensation when passing urine and an increased frequency of micturition.
explanation: Lower urinary tract infection first-line treatment is nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim.

question: A 30-year-old presents with a rash on her thigh where she was bitten by an insect 3 weeks previously. On examination, the rash has got a central pale area.
explanation: Rash with central pallor after insect bite suggests Lyme disease. Doxycycline is first-line treatment.

question: A 30-year-old woman presents with fever and a sore throat. On examination, she has got a white exudate on her tonsils.
explanation: Bacterial tonsillitis with white exudate is treated with penicillin V (phenoxymethylpenicillin).

question: A couple have been trying to conceive for the past 6 months

options.g: Day two oestradiol of the cycle

explanation: Chlamydia infection can cause subfertility. Screening for Chlamydia is first investigation.

question: A 28-year-old lady has been trying to conceive for the past 4 months. She has a history of chlamydia infection in the past.

options.g: Day two oestradiol of the cycle

explanation: History of PID suggests tubal blockage. Laparoscopy and dye test is recommended for women with comorbidities like PID.

question: A 30-year-old lady with subfertility presents with pain during sexual intercourse. She also complains of painful menstrual periods

options.g: Day two oestradiol of the cycle

explanation: Pain during intercourse and painful periods with subfertility suggests endometriosis. Laparoscopy is investigation of choice.

question: A 19-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with asthma attends for review. He uses salbutamol inhaler 3 times daily as instructed
explanation: Frequent salbutamol use indicates poor control. NICE recommends adding inhaled corticosteroid (beclomethasone).

question: A 31-year-old man with asthma is on salmeterol/fluticasone 25/250mg. Recently he has been using his salbutamol inhaler very frequently.
explanation: Poor control despite ICS/LABA requires short course of oral prednisolone for acute exacerbation.

question: A 46-year-old woman presents with flushing and diarrhoea.
explanation: Flushing and diarrhea are classic carcinoid syndrome symptoms from serotonin-secreting tumor.

question: A 56-year-old man experiences dizziness and sweating after meals.
explanation: Dizziness and sweating after meals is classic for dumping syndrome after gastric surgery.

question: A 42-year-old man with central obesity and abdominal striae.
explanation: Central obesity with abdominal striae is classic for Cushing's syndrome from excess cortisol.

question: A 35-year-old lady presents with headaches. She was recently at a wine tasting event.
explanation: Metronidazole causes disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, causing headache, flushing, nausea even with small amounts of alcohol.

question: A 27-year-old pregnant woman develops intense jerking of her jaws and intense upwards deviation of her eyes.
explanation: Acute dystonic reaction with oculogyric crises is classic side effect of metoclopramide, especially in young women.

question: A 61-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation develops haematuria. He has had fever and cough with green sputum in the last few days.
explanation: Clarithromycin is macrolide antibiotic for pneumonia. Macrolides inhibit P450 enzyme, potentiating warfarin and causing haematuria.

question: A 22-year-old man presents with hyperpigmentation of oral mucosa and dizziness.
explanation: Hyperpigmentation of oral mucosa and dizziness suggests Addison's disease. Synacthen test is diagnostic.

question: A 43-year-old man has visual disturbances and headaches.
explanation: Visual disturbances and headaches suggest pituitary mass. Prolactinoma is most common. Prolactin levels should be measured.

question: A 12-month-old baby develops diarrhoea and irritability. Her mother is still breastfeeding her.
explanation: Breastfed baby with diarrhea likely has gastroenteritis-related lactose intolerance; low dairy helps symptoms.

question: A 46-year-old man presents with bloating and abdominal pain which is relieved by defecation.
explanation: Bloating and pain relieved by defecation suggests IBS. Low-FODMAP diet reduces fermentable carbohydrates that cause symptoms.

question: A 57-year-old woman develops abdominal pain, weight loss, bloating and constipation with alternating diarrhoea. The symptoms are worse after certain food.
explanation: Weight loss, bloating, alternating bowel habit with food triggers suggests coeliac disease requiring gluten-free diet.

question: A 19-year-old girl develop spots on her face, upper chest and back
explanation: Teenager with spots on face, chest and back is classic acne vulgaris affecting pilosebaceous follicles.

question: A 22-year-old man develops redness after exposure to heat and after eating spicy food.
explanation: Facial flushing triggered by heat and spicy foods is characteristic of rosacea, a chronic vasodilatory condition.

question: A 22-year-old man is found to have a blistering rash on both of his knees. He has weight loss and low haemoglobin.
explanation: Blistering rash on knees with weight loss and anemia suggests dermatitis herpetiformis associated with coeliac disease.

question: A 37-year-old woman presents with a plaque in her neck, side of the nose, eyebrows axillae and groin. The lesions are itchy and improved during summer times
explanation: Itchy plaques in skin folds (neck, nose, eyebrows, axillae, groin) improving in summer suggests seborrheic eczema.

question: A 32-year-old lady presents with shortness of breath. Chest is clear. The patient is talking normally and tells you she is fine.
explanation: Clear chest examination with SOB and normal speech is typical for PE. Other causes would have abnormal chest findings.

question: An 80-year-old woman from the nursing home develops blistering, tense blisters on the chest and trunk. She has no oral mucosal lesions.
explanation: Elderly with tense bullae on trunk without oral involvement is classic for bullous pemphigoid, an autoimmune blistering disease.

question: A 32-year-old woman presents with anxiety, palpitations and tremors in the hands. She has clinically proven hyperthyroidism.
explanation: Immediate symptom control in hyperthyroidism requires beta-blocker like propranolol for anxiety, palpitations, and tremors.

question: A 19-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with acute onset of shortness of breath and an itchy rash. He had used his own auto-injection of adrenaline. He is now feeling well.

options.d: Keep him in the department for observation for 6 hours

explanation: After anaphylaxis treatment, observation for 6-12 hours is required to monitor for biphasic reaction.

question: A 48-year-old woman with diabetes type II is found to have a clinic blood pressure of 138/85mmHg.
explanation: Clinic BP 138/85 is borderline. ABPM is needed to confirm diagnosis of hypertension before treatment.

question: A 65-year-old woman with a history of atrial fibrillation presents with a sudden loss of vision.
explanation: Sudden vision loss in AF patient suggests retinal artery embolism causing amaurosis fugax (curtain descending).

question: A 60-year-old man woke up this morning with hearing loss. Rinne's test is louder when placed in front of the ear bilaterally. Weber's lateralizes to the right.
explanation: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is ENT emergency needing urgent assessment within 24 hours.

question: A 36-year-old woman presents with low mood, insomnia and loss of interest in her daily activities.
explanation: Depression first-line treatment is SSRI. Citalopram is the only SSRI among options.

question: A 46-year-old man develops pain in the thumb, 2nd and 3rd fingers.
explanation: Pain in thumb, 2nd and 3rd fingers suggests carpal tunnel syndrome. Nerve conduction studies are gold standard test.

question: A 60-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with giant cell arteritis presents with muscle weakness of the lower limb. On examination, he has wasting of the muscle
explanation: Muscle weakness and wasting is common side effect of long-term steroid therapy used for giant cell arteritis.

question: A 65-year-old man has nocturia and tiredness. He has recently developed erectile dysfunction.
explanation: Nocturia, tiredness, and erectile dysfunction suggest diabetes mellitus. HbA1c is diagnostic test.

question: A 3-year-old boy has developed multiple umbilicated lesions on his trunk and extremities.
explanation: Multiple umbilicated lesions in a child is molluscum contagiosum. It's self-limiting, usually resolving in 18 months.

question: A 19-year-old man with a history of hay fever presents with shortness of breath and wheeze. He is unable to speak in full sentences. He has had a fever, cough and running nose recently
explanation: Unable to speak in full sentences indicates severe asthma exacerbation. Nebulized salbutamol is immediate treatment.

question: A 28-year-old man is found to have a raised alanine transferase. His dad died of liver problems. All his family members have been advised to get screened
explanation: Family history of liver disease suggests hereditary hemochromatosis. Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation) are screening tests.

question: A 77-year-old man presents with shortness of breath, cough and weight loss.
explanation: Elderly smoker with SOB, cough and weight loss is classic presentation of lung cancer until proven otherwise.

question: A 2-year-old child presents with cough and fever. On examination, he has widespread crackles.
explanation: Widespread crackles in a 2-year-old with cough/fever is bronchiolitis. Pneumonia has localized crackles.note tht ideally bronchiolitis occurs before 2 years of age

question: A 66-year-old woman presents with chronic back pain. She has sacroilitis on X-ray. The straight leg test is 40 degrees bilaterally. Blood results are as follows: Hb 11.5 (13.5-16), MCV 88 (80-100), Na+ 138 (135-145), K+ 4 (3.5-5), Ca2+ 2.75 (2.12-2.65), Urea 4 (2.5-6.5), Creatinine 180 (60-120), ESR 57 (10-30)
explanation: Anemia, high ESR, hypercalcemia, high creatinine with back pain suggests multiple myeloma. Sacroilitis is misleading.

question: A 77-year-old woman presents with weight loss. Haemoglobin is 10.5g/L (normal 13.5-16g/L).
explanation: Weight loss with unexplained anemia in elderly suggests colorectal cancer causing occult bleeding.

question: A 48-year-old man presents with burning pains in both of his legs.
explanation: Burning pain suggests neuropathic pain. Duloxetine is licensed for neuropathic pain treatment.

question: A 70-year-old man woke up this morning with visual problems. He has homonymous hemianopia.
explanation: Sudden homonymous hemianopia indicates stroke. Requires urgent hospital admission for investigation and treatment.

question: A 28-year-old man presents with acute left eye pain and visual loss. Two years ago he had weakness in his right arm which resolved within one month

options.c: Computerised tomography scan of the brain

explanation: Acute optic neuritis with history of resolved arm weakness suggests multiple sclerosis. MRI is investigation of choice.

question: A 35-year-old man presents with painful itchy small multiple pustules on the chin and cheeks. Which got worse a few days after shaving.
explanation: Multiple pustules on beard area worse after shaving is folliculitis, infection of hair follicles.

question: A 56-year-old man with a history of hypertension, diabetes and peptic ulcer develops angioedema. Which of the following medications needs to be stopped?
explanation: ACE inhibitors like lisinopril cause angioedema. Should be stopped immediately and never restarted.

question: A two-year-old child has a cough and stridor. His symptoms improve during the day.
explanation: Viral croup causes cough and stridor improving during day. Single dose oral dexamethasone is treatment.

question: A 29-year-old man presents with loin pain. Temperature 36.8 degrees celsius. Urine dipstick shows blood +++. Leucocytes are negative and nitrites are negative.
explanation: Loin pain with hematuria but no pyuria/nitrites suggests renal stone, not infection.

question: A 2-year-old child presents with cough and fever. On examination, he has widespread crackles.
explanation: Widespread crackles in a 2-year-old with cough/fever is bronchiolitis. Pneumonia has localized crackles.

question: A 10-year-old boy is brought with ear pain which has persisted for about 24 hours.
explanation: Acute otitis media often viral. No antibiotics needed for mild cases <4 days. Treat pain, observe.

question: A 40-year-old woman has had headaches for the past 4 months. She sees zig-zag dots while typing before the headaches.
explanation: Migraine with visual aura (zig-zag dots) before headache is classic. Chronic recurrent pattern.

question: A 29-year-old man with schizophrenia develops tremors and akathisia after being prescribed some medications. Which of the following medications is the most likely cause?
explanation: Haloperidol is typical antipsychotic causing extrapyramidal side effects like tremor and akathisia.

question: 60-year-old man presents with shoulder and arm pain when he extends his neck
explanation: Shoulder/arm pain with neck extension suggests cervical radiculopathy. MRI is investigation of choice for neurological symptoms. according to nice - cervical imaging is not routinely required to diagnose neck pain with radiculopatyhy. mri is indicated in poeple with complex cervical radiculopathy eg. abscess or failure to improve after 4-6 weeks of conservative treatment

question: A 35-year-old man experiences pain at the bottom of his foot and when he steps down. When he walks, the pain even becomes worse.
explanation: According to nice guidelines plantar fascitis is usually diagnosed by history and physical examinations alone.

question: A 39-year-old woman presents with pain in the joints of the fingers of both hands
explanation: Bilateral symmetrical small joint pain in hands in a woman suggests rheumatoid arthritis.

question: A 30-year-old woman presents with lower abdominal pain. Her last menstrual period was 7 weeks ago. On examination, she has left iliac fossa tenderness. Blood pressure is 90/60 and heart rate is 120bpm.
explanation: Hypotension and tachycardia with LIF pain and amenorrhea suggests ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Immediate IV access for resuscitation is priority.

question: An 83-year-old woman with osteoarthritis has wrist pains. She has tried paracetamol but with little relief.
explanation: Osteoarthritis pain not controlled by paracetamol. Topical NSAIDs should be tried before oral NSAIDs to reduce systemic side effects.

question: You have just got the news that there is an outbreak of H7N7 parainfluenza. Your family is asking you what to do. The outbreak is 10 miles away from where they live.

options.a: All family members should get vaccinated
options.b: All the family members should not eat eggs

explanation: For disease outbreak, avoiding travel to affected area is key preventive measure. No specific treatment mentioned.

question: A 35-year-old woman, who has had varicose veins for years develops pain and swelling of the left calf. The circumference of the left leg is 2cm more than that of the right leg.
explanation: Unilateral calf swelling with pain in patient with varicose veins is DVT until proven otherwise. Needs urgent assessment.

question: An 83-year-old lady has been found to have white cells in the urine. She has no symptoms.
explanation: Asymptomatic bacteriuria in elderly requires no treatment unless pregnant or undergoing urological procedure.

question: A 35-year-old woman has palpitations, anxiety and gritty sensation in the eyes
explanation: Palpitations, anxiety with gritty eye sensation suggests Graves' disease with thyroid eye disease.

question: A 4-year-old child has had two episodes of urinary tract infection.

options.d: X-ray of the kidney ureter and bladder

explanation: Recurrent UTI in children >3 years requires ultrasound scan within 6 weeks to identify structural abnormalities.

question: A 16-year-old girl is on treatment for acne. She has been experiencing flushing of her face.
explanation: Doxycycline commonly causes photosensitivity and flushing as side effect.

question: A 62-year-old man presents with dizziness. On examination he has got a murmur.
explanation: Murmur suggests valvular heart disease. Echocardiogram is investigation of choice for valvular pathology.

question: A 40-year-old man develops sudden onset of headache while exercising. It is the worse headache of his life
explanation: Sudden severe 'worst headache' during exertion is classic for subarachnoid haemorrhage from ruptured aneurysm.

question: A 19-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and wheeze. During a similar episode previously he had a negative IgE. He is unable to breathe completely.
explanation: SOB/wheeze with negative IgE suggests hereditary angioedema. C1 esterase inhibitor is specific treatment.

question: A 47-year-old man presents with abdominal pains, dark urine and pale stools.
explanation: Dark urine, pale stools, abdominal pain suggests obstructive jaundice. Ultrasound is first-line investigation for gallstones.

question: A 32-year-old woman is found to have haematuria. Her brothers died of a brain haemorrhage. On examination, she has a mass on the right flank
explanation: Family history of brain hemorrhage and flank mass suggests adult polycystic kidney disease with associated berry aneurysms.

question: A 10-year-old boy is found to have hypertension. On urinalysis, he has blood (++) and protein (+)
explanation: Hypertension with hematuria and proteinuria in a child suggests glomerulonephritis.

question: A 10-year-old boy presents with swelling of the legs bilaterally. On urinalysis, he has protein (+++).
explanation: Bilateral leg swelling with heavy proteinuria (+++) indicates nephrotic syndrome, commonly minimal change disease in children.

question: A 45-year-old woman, who has had varicose veins for years develops pain and swelling of the left calf. The circumference of the left leg is 2cm more than that of the right leg.
explanation: Unilateral calf swelling with pain in patient with varicose veins is DVT until proven otherwise. Needs urgent assessment.

question: A 62 year-old woman with a history of diabetes, hypertension, osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis complains of chronic shortness of breath. On examination, she has bilateral inspiratory crackles.
explanation: Methotrexate causes pulmonary fibrosis in rheumatoid arthritis patients, presenting with chronic dyspnea and bilateral crackles.

question: A 10 year-old boy has a fever and sore throat but no cough. On examination, he has exudate on his tonsils
explanation: Bacterial tonsillitis suggested by fever, sore throat, exudate, no cough. Phenoxymethylpenicillin is first-line treatment.

question: A 30 year-old woman has fever, sore throat and cough for the past 4 days. On examination there is non-exudate exfoliation of the tonsils
explanation: Viral tonsillitis suggested by fever, sore throat, cough, non-exudative tonsils. No antibiotics needed.

question: A 51 year-old man has bilateral ptosis which worsens after exercise
explanation: Myasthenia Gravis causes fatigable bilateral ptosis worsening with exercise. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies confirm diagnosis.

question: A 56 year-old man presents with left sided headache, vision loss and ptosis for the past two months
explanation: Brain tumor causing 3rd nerve palsy suggested by chronic unilateral headache, vision loss, ptosis. CT scan diagnoses.

question: A 53 year-old man is found to have wasting of the thenar eminence muscles.

options.e: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh

explanation: Thenar muscle wasting indicates median nerve injury. Median nerve supplies thenar muscles (LOAF).

question: A 42 year-old lady is found to have wasting of the hypothenar muscles.

options.e: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh

explanation: Hypothenar muscle wasting indicates ulnar nerve injury. Ulnar nerve supplies hypothenar eminence.

question: A 60 year-old man presents with burning pain on the lateral side of the thigh. The pain is aggravated by standing and relieved on sitting.

options.e: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh

explanation: Lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh entrapment causes burning pain on lateral thigh, worse standing, better sitting.

question: A 6 year-old boy develops brown crusted lesion around his mouth and nose. He has infected some of his friends in the class.
explanation: Impetigo causes brown crusted lesions around mouth/nose in children, highly contagious to classmates.

question: An 89 year-old woman presents with a tingling sensation on her right thigh. On further questioning, she also has burning pain on the right side of her back.
explanation: Shingles causes tingling/burning pain following dermatomal distribution in elderly. Vesicular rash appears later.

question: A 73 year-old woman presents with a dark lesion on her chest. She has had the lesion for a very long time. On examination, the lesion has a "stuck on" appearance and looks greasy.
explanation: Seborrheic keratosis in elderly has "stuck on" greasy appearance, long duration, benign.

question: A 10 year-old boy has well-defined patches of erythema associated with flaking of the skin on his scalp. On examination, he has got dandruff.
explanation: Seborrheic dermatitis causes erythematous flaky patches on scalp with dandruff, common in children.

question: A 30 year-old woman who has a 3 year-old child presents with pain in the wrist. She has tenderness at the base of the thumb.
explanation: De Quervain tenosynovitis causes tenderness at radial styloid, worse with lifting child. First extensor compartment involved.

question: A 30 year-old pregnant woman develops pains in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th fingers and wrist. The pains are worse at night.
explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome in pregnancy causes pain/tingling in thumb, index, middle, radial half of ring finger, worse at night.

question: A 49 year-old lady frequently gets her ring finger locked after bending the fingers. She has to pull it with the other hand in order to straighten it and while doing that she hears a popping sound.
explanation: Trigger finger (stenosing tenosynovitis) causes locking of finger in flexion, needs passive extension with pop sound.

sub-category: Obstetrics and Gynaecology - Diagnosis of vaginal discharge
question: A 35 year-old lady presents with thin, fishy, smelly vaginal discharge. Microscopy reveals clue cells.
explanation: Bacterial vaginosis causes thin fishy discharge with clue cells on microscopy, pH >4.5.

sub-category: Obstetrics and Gynaecology - Diagnosis of vaginal discharge
question: A 45 year-old woman with diabetes mellitus presents with vulvar discomfort. On examination, there is erythema and fissuring of the vulva.
explanation: Candidiasis causes vulvar erythema, fissuring, especially in diabetics. Presents with itching and white discharge.

question: A 62 year-old man has generalized weakness. He is unable to stand up from the chair on his own. He needs to hold onto the wall in order to stand. FBC, urea and electrolytes, creatinine and creatinine kinase are all normal.
explanation: Polymyalgia rheumatica causes proximal muscle weakness, difficulty rising from chair, normal CK, in patients >50 years.

question: A 60 year-old man presents with muscle aches and weakness. FBC, urea and electrolytes are all normal. Creatinine kinase is high
explanation: Polymyositis causes muscle aches, weakness, and markedly elevated CK (>10x normal), unlike polymyalgia rheumatica.

question: A 35 year-old woman has bilateral conductive hearing loss. The external auditory canal is normal.
explanation: Otosclerosis causes bilateral conductive hearing loss in young adults, often with family history. Usually normal otoscopy.

question: A 10 year-old boy had severe ear pain which resolved following a thick discharge from the ear.
explanation: Tympanic membrane perforation causes sudden relief of severe ear pain after discharge. Often follows acute otitis media.

question: A 42 year-old man with hypertension and muscle weakness. Potassium is 3.1mmol/L (range: 3.5-5mmol/L)
explanation: Conn's syndrome (hyperaldosteronism) causes hypertension and hypokalemia leading to muscle weakness.

sub-category: Gastroenterology - Diagnosis of shortness of breath
question: A 23 year-old woman presents with cough for the past 8 months. She has clear sputum.
explanation: GERD causes chronic cough with clear sputum. Acid reflux irritates airways, more likely in absence of other signs.

question: A 35 year-old woman presents with weight loss and palpitations. On examination her heart rate is 102 and her blood pressure is high.
explanation: Hyperthyroidism causes weight loss, palpitations, tachycardia, hypertension. TSH and T4 testing confirms diagnosis.

question: A 41-year-old woman presents with palpitations and sweating. She has hypertension and a heart rate of 102. Her weight is stable
explanation: Pheochromocytoma causes palpitations, sweating, hypertension, stable weight. 24-hour urinary catecholamines/metanephrines confirm.

question: A 35 year-old lady with Bipolar Disorder has been prescribed Lithium.

options.c: Liver function tests and urea and electrolytes

explanation: Lithium is renally excreted. Baseline and regular U&E monitoring (every 6 months) essential to check renal function and avoid toxicity. before starting lithium you should do u&e, tft, lithium. lithium every 3 months, the other two every 6 months

question: A 30 year-old presents with a thin yellow frothy vaginal discharge
explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis causes thin yellow frothy discharge with strawberry cervix. Treated with metronidazole 400-500mg for 5-7 days.

question: A 30 year-old woman presents with itchy white vaginal discharge. She has recently completed treatment for a dental abscess.
explanation: Candidiasis causes itchy white discharge, often after antibiotics. Topical clotrimazole cream or oral fluconazole is first-line treatment.

question: A 30 year-old woman presents with dysuria. On examination she has multiple genital painful ulcers.
explanation: Genital herpes causes multiple painful ulcers. Treated with oral acyclovir 400mg TDS for 7-10 days.

question: A 73 year-old man with a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus type 2 and myocardial infarction is found to have a heart rate of 40.
explanation: Beta-blockers like atenolol cause bradycardia. History of MI and hypertension suggests beta-blocker use, causing HR of 40.

question: A 60 year-old man with history of hypertension, benign prostate hyperplasia and diabetes is found to have bilateral swelling of the legs.
explanation: Calcium channel blockers like amlodipine commonly cause peripheral edema. Used for hypertension, can cause bilateral leg swelling.

question: A 30 year-old lady presents with tiredness and muscle weakness. She has a history of diabetes, hypertension, gastroesophageal reflux disease and myocardial infarction.
explanation: Omeprazole can cause tiredness and muscle weakness as side effects. Commonly used for GERD.

question: A 70 year-old woman develops itchy dry skin in the hands, legs and trunk which gets worse in winter.
explanation: Asteatotic eczema in elderly causes dry, itchy skin on hands, legs, trunk worsening in winter due to decreased skin lipids.

question: A 61 year-old woman has dry scaly patches on both of her lower limbs. On examination, she has got a round erythematous plaques.
explanation: Discoid eczema causes round erythematous plaques on lower limbs, common in adults 15-25 and 50-65 years age groups.

question: A 4 year-old boy has had wheeze for the past 4 weeks. On examination, he has got a monophonic wheeze on the upper right zone.
explanation: Foreign body aspiration causes focal monophonic wheeze in children. Asthma would cause bilateral polyphonic wheeze.

question: A 30 year-old woman presents with bilateral lumpiness and pain in the breast. The pain seems to worsen before the start of her menstruation period
explanation: Fibrocystic disease causes bilateral breast pain and lumpiness that worsens premenstrually due to hormonal changes.

question: A 60 year-old woman presents with a lump in her left breast. On examination, she has a palpable lymph node in the left axilla.
explanation: Breast cancer in elderly presents with breast lump and axillary lymphadenopathy suggesting metastasis.

question: A 38-year-old man who had thyroidectomy presents with tingling sensation in the hands. On assessment he has carpal pedal spasm.
explanation: Thyroidectomy can damage parathyroid glands causing hypocalcemia, leading to tingling and carpopedal spasm. Calcium gluconate treats this.

question: A 72-year-old man presents with rash on the thigh. He also has a tingling sensation on the same area. His cat has got fleas and he has noticed that the cat has been scratching itself.
explanation: Cat scratch disease from Bartonella henselae causes rash and tingling. Associated with flea-infested cats.

question: A 62-year-old man is on several medication for gout, osteoarthritis, hypertension and ischemic heart disease and gastroesophageal reflux disease. He presents with shortness of breath and on examination he has bilateral crackles
explanation: NSAIDs like naproxen worsen heart failure. Bilateral crackles indicate pulmonary edema from heart failure exacerbation.

question: A 61-year-old man has had recurrent balanitis for the past 3 months. He is unable to retract his foreskin.

options.b: Advice to keep trying to retract the foreskin

explanation: Recurrent balanitis with phimosis requires specialist referral. May need circumcision. Urology/dermatology referral appropriate. according to nice guidelines phimosis could be caused by recurrent balinitis and first line management is steroids. if it fails, refer to urologist.

question: A 65-year-old man presents with central crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm
explanation: MI management starts with aspirin 300mg loading dose. Immediate antiplatelet therapy is first-line for acute coronary syndrome.

question: A 66-year-old man who is taking warfarin for deep venous thrombosis presents with mild bruise on the arms. His INR is 8.4 and warfarin has been stopped.

options.a: IM phytomenadione and review in 48 hours

explanation: INR >8 with minor bleeding: stop warfarin, give oral vitamin K (phytomenadione), recheck INR, restart when INR <5.

question: A 19-month-old child is brought to the emergency department with fever for 2 days. Ear examination shows red bulging tympanic membrane on the left side. The baby is allergic to penicillin.
explanation: Acute otitis media <4 days duration doesn't need antibiotics. Paracetamol for fever/pain sufficient. Only 2 days of symptoms.

question: A 31-year-old man was involved in an accident. He is unconscious and the GCS is 4.
explanation: GCS ≤8 indicates airway compromise. Endotracheal intubation is required to protect airway in severe head injury.

question: A 21-year-old afro-Caribbean woman with fibroids requests for contraception advice. She has been on combined contraceptive pill, but she has been forgetting to take her pills frequently. She has menorrhagia
explanation: Mirena IUS is ideal for menorrhagia and fibroids. Provides contraception and reduces bleeding. More reliable than forgotten pills.

question: A 47-year-old woman with abdominal striae and weight gain. On examination she has a buffalo hump.
explanation: Cushing's syndrome features. Synacthen (ACTH stimulation) test diagnoses adrenal insufficiency vs Cushing's. Best initial test which could be either daytime and beditme salivary cortisol, 2-24hours urinary cortisol, low dose dexamethasone supression test

question: A 44-year-old woman presents with polyuria and polydipsia. Calcium level is 3.4mmol/L.

options.d: Advice to drink a lot of water

explanation: Hypercalcemia (3.4 mmol/L) causes polyuria and polydipsia. Check PTH to determine if primary hyperparathyroidism is cause.

question: An elderly man has been on treatment for urinary tract infection with antibiotics for the past 7 days. She has developed profuse diarrhea.
explanation: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea suggests C. difficile infection. Metronidazole is first-line treatment for C. difficile colitis.

question: An 87-year-old lady is brought from the nursing home with itchy rashes in between her fingers of both hands. Other residents of the nursing home have been similarly affected and have received treatment.
explanation: Scabies causes itchy rash between fingers, spreads in close contacts like nursing home residents. Burrows and nocturnal itching characteristic.

question: A 32-year-old man presents with low back pain which radiates to the right leg. He is unable to lift his right leg off the floor and cannot control his bladder.

options.e: Urgent MRI scan of the spine

explanation: Cauda equina syndrome suggested by back pain, leg weakness, bladder dysfunction. Requires urgent neurosurgical referral for decompression.

question: A 22-year-old man has noticed tanning of his skin. His lab investigations are as follows. Hb 15.2, MCV 90, Na+ 137, K+ 5.7, Urea 4.4, Creatinine 98
explanation: Addison's disease causes hyperpigmentation (tanning) and hyperkalemia (K+ 5.7). Presents with fatigue, hypotension.

question: A 62 year-old man with a history of benign prostate hyperplasia, diabetes mellitus, angina and osteoporosis presents with dizziness.
explanation: Tamsulosin (alpha-blocker) for BPH causes orthostatic hypotension leading to dizziness, especially in elderly.

question: A 5 year-old boy has a fever and a red rash on both cheeks. What is the most appropriate action?

options.b: Advise not to go to school

explanation: No school exclusion in slapped cheek syndrome, specifically after appearance of rash as child is no longer infectious.

question: A 25 year-old woman presents with vesicular lesions on her vulva

options.a: Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) for syphilis

explanation: Genital vesicular lesions suggest herpes simplex. PCR testing of vesicle fluid or ulcer base confirms HSV diagnosis.

question: A 69 year-old man who is a smoker develops severe intense pain and swelling below his knee.
explanation: DVT causes unilateral leg pain and swelling. Risk factors: age >60, smoking, immobility, cancer.

question: A 47 year-old woman presents with a raised shiny scaly lesion on the labia minora.
explanation: Lichen planus causes raised, shiny, scaly lesions on vulva with violaceous papules and Wickham's striae. Potent topical steroids treat.

question: A 16 year-old girl requests for contraception. Her periods are irregular and heavy.
explanation: COCP regulates menstrual cycle, reduces heavy bleeding. Ideal for adolescents with menorrhagia/irregular periods who can adhere to daily pills.

question: A 35 year-old man gets severe pain when he gets erection. The skin of his penis has got a fissure and it is whitish in colour. The pain is so severe that it makes him cry.
explanation: Candida balanitis causes severe pain on erection, white fissured lesions on glans. Common in diabetics, after antibiotics.

question: A 47-year-old woman presents with a raised shiny scaly lesion on the labia minora
explanation: Lichen planus on vulva treated with potent topical steroids like clobetasol propionate cream. Resolves spontaneously in 6-9 months.

question: A 79 year-old woman with Alzheimer's disease has been noticed by her husband to be more confused in the last few days. She has been wandering around and has become abusive to her husband.
explanation: Delirium is acute confusion with altered consciousness in elderly with dementia. UTI common cause. Presents with agitation, wandering.

question: A 10 year-old boy develops cyclical abdominal pain which develops almost every week
explanation: Abdominal migraine causes recurrent cyclical abdominal pain in children. Diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out organic causes. No treatment needed.

question: A 67 year-old man is unable to lift his hand above his head. He has shoulder and hip stiffness.
explanation: Polymyalgia rheumatica causes proximal muscle stiffness. Treated with prednisolone 15mg daily for 3 weeks, then taper over 1-2 years.

question: A 46 year-old man present with tiredness, day time somnolence and fatigue. His BMI is 38kg/m2.
explanation: Obstructive sleep apnea suspected in obese patient with daytime sleepiness. Epworth Sleepiness Scale assesses OSA severity and need for investigation. osas usually presents with high bmi and daytime sleepiness. hypothyroidism in adition to this may include constipation, subfertility (males), thinning hair, dry skin

question: A young boy is diagnosed with Perthe's disease following after he had hip pain. What is the typical age of onset of Perthe's disease?
explanation: Perthe's disease (avascular necrosis of femoral head) typically occurs in children aged 3-8 years, more common in boys.

question: A 56 year-old man who works at the farm presents with dry cough.
explanation: Extrinsic allergic alveolitis (hypersensitivity pneumonitis) causes dry cough in farmers exposed to moldy hay. Presents 4-6 hours after exposure.

question: A 28 year-old man with a history of diabetes has noticed that his skin has been getting tanned. His sister is being investigated for the same problem.
explanation: Hereditary hemochromatosis (autosomal recessive) causes bronze skin pigmentation, diabetes, family history. Iron deposition in skin and pancreas.

question: A 42 year-old woman has pains in both hands, especially in the interphalangeal joint. She is positive for a particular antibody.
explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis causes symmetrical small joint pain. Positive rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP antibodies confirm diagnosis.

question: A 4 year-old boy presents with haematuria. He has recently had sore throat.
explanation: IgA nephropathy presents with hematuria 2-4 days after URTI sore throat. Post-streptococcal GN occurs 2-3 weeks later.

question: An 85 year-old woman presents with visual loss and weakness on her left arm which lasted a few minutes.
explanation: Transient ischemic attack lasts <24 hours. Immediate aspirin 300mg reduces risk of subsequent stroke. Needs urgent referral.

question: A 35 year-old man has a problem maintaining his erection. He is in a new relationship. He had no problems in his previous relationship.
explanation: Performance anxiety causes erectile dysfunction in new relationships. Previous normal function rules out organic causes. Psychosexual counseling helps.

question: A 2 year-old boy is brought to the hospital by his mother with fever, drooling of saliva and hoarseness of voice.
explanation: Acute epiglottitis causes fever, drooling, hoarse voice in children. Medical emergency requiring airway protection and antibiotics.

question: An 8 year-old boy complains of hip pain during activities.
explanation: Perthe's disease (3-10 years) causes hip pain. SUFE occurs in adolescents 10-16. OA and RA unlikely in children.

question: A 36 year-old woman was bitten in the forest by an insect while she was camping. She presents with a rash on her leg. The rash has got a pale central area.
explanation: Lyme disease from tick bite causes erythema migrans: target lesion with pale center. Test for Borrelia Burgdorferi antibodies.

question: A 17 year-old boy presents with acute testicular pain. On examination, there is scrotal swelling.
explanation: Acute testicular pain in adolescent is torsion until proven otherwise. Requires emergency urology admission for exploration within 6 hours.

question: A 45 year-old man has a swelling on the back of his wrist. The lesion can be slightly painful at times.
explanation: Ganglion cyst on wrist dorsum. If painful, refer routinely to orthopaedics for aspiration or surgical removal.

question: A 26 year-old man from Greece is found to have a haemoglobin level of 11 (normal: 13.5-16 g/dL) on routine check-up.
explanation: Thalassemia trait common in Mediterranean population. Causes mild anemia (Hb 9-11) with normal MCV/RBC indices.

question: A 16 year-old boy presents with left testicular pain. The cremasteric reflex is absent.
explanation: Absent cremasteric reflex highly suggests testicular torsion. Emergency urology admission needed within 6 hours to save testis.

question: An 80 year-old elderly woman presents with weight loss and change in bowel habit. She is not suitable for endoscopy due to co-morbidities.
explanation: CT colonography is alternative to colonoscopy for colorectal cancer diagnosis when endoscopy contraindicated. Detects polyps and masses.

question: A 60 year-old man who is a chronic smoker presents with weight loss. Chest X-ray shows a circular opacity in the left upper lobe.
explanation: Smoking + weight loss + solitary pulmonary nodule = lung cancer until proven otherwise. Needs urgent referral and staging.

question: A 45 year-old man developed sudden back pain while lifting some heavy objects. He has localized lower back pain.

options.b: Simple analgesia and advice to mobilize

explanation: Acute mechanical back pain from lifting. Treat with simple analgesia and encourage mobility. Bed rest no longer recommended.

question: A 56 year-old farmer presents with fever, headache and myalgia. He has lymphadenopathy.
explanation: Brucellosis from infected livestock causes fever, headache, myalgia, lymphadenopathy in farmers. Chronic granulomatous disease.

question: A 5 year-old girl brought to the GP surgery by her mother with ear discharge. The mother says her daughter had had severe pain which aborted following discharge from the ear. She also mentions that her child has had fever in the last 3 days.
explanation: Acute otitis media causing severe pain that resolves after tympanic membrane rupture and discharge is classic. Treat with analgesics.

question: A 60 year-old man develops painful pale fingers when he walks in the cold weather. His fingers turn red and painful on rewarming.
explanation: Beta-blockers worsen Raynaud's phenomenon causing cold-induced vasospasm. Causes painful pale fingers that turn red on rewarming.

question: A 25 year-old lady presents with a 20 month-history of amenorrhea. Luteinizing hormone and Follicle-stimulating hormone are high. Oestrogen is low.
explanation: Premature ovarian insufficiency: amenorrhea <40 years, high FSH/LH, low estrogen. Causes infertility, menopausal symptoms.

question: A 29 year-old develops thin white vaginal discharge which has a fishy odour.
explanation: Bacterial vaginosis causes thin white fishy discharge. Treated with oral metronidazole 400mg twice daily for 5-7 days.

question: A 14 year-old girl requests an emergency contraception pill following unprotected sexual intercourse 12 hours ago.
explanation: Emergency contraceptive pills (levonorgestrel, ulipristal) inhibit or delay ovulation. Must be taken within 72-120 hours of intercourse.

question: A 49 year-old woman develops pinprick sensation on her face.
explanation: Trigeminal neuralgia causes facial pain. Carbamazepine is first-line treatment. Diagnosis is clinical based on characteristic shooting pain.

question: A 36 year-old woman presents with irregular periods, acne, and obesity.
explanation: PCOS causes irregular periods, acne, obesity, hirsutism. Rotterdam criteria: oligomenorrhea, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound.

question: A 10-year-old girl presents with dribbling of urine. On examination, she has adhesion of the labia minor.
explanation: Labial fusion in prepubertal girls causes urinary dribbling. Topical estrogen cream applied for 4-6 weeks separates labia effectively.

question: A 62 year-old man who has smoked 40 sticks of cigarette a day for the last 40 years has progressive hoarseness of voice for the past three months.
explanation: Chronic smoking + persistent hoarseness >3 weeks suggests laryngeal cancer. Urgent ENT referral for laryngoscopy and biopsy needed.

question: A 16 year-old girl has taken an overdose of paracetamol tablets. In which of the following situations will you treat with N-acetyl cysteine without considering the time of ingestion of paracetamol?
explanation: Staggered overdose renders paracetamol nomogram unreliable. Give N-acetylcysteine immediately regardless of timing due to uncertain ingestion.

question: A 30 year-old lady who delivered 20 days ago via c-section requests contraception.
explanation: Postpartum <21 days: progestogen-only pill safe for non-breastfeeding women. Combined pill contraindicated due to VTE risk.

question: A 41 year-old woman presents with cough and fever. On examination, she has a rash on her leg which has a pale area between the dark centre and round red border.
explanation: Mycoplasma pneumonia causes atypical pneumonia with erythema multiforme rash (target lesions with pale center). Treated with macrolides.

question: A 69 year-old lady who is terminally ill with breast cancer develops chest pain. On examination, there is a rash on the chest which extends to her back.
explanation: Immunocompromised cancer patients at risk for shingles reactivation. Rash follows dermatomal distribution (chest to back), very painful.

question: A 60 year-old lady with a history of osteoporosis, diabetes and ischaemic heart disease has developed indigestion.
explanation: Bisphosphonates (for osteoporosis) commonly cause esophagitis and indigestion. Must be taken with water, upright for 30 minutes.

question: A 36-year-old woman has weight gain, dry mouth, constipation and gritty sensation in the eyes.
explanation: Hashimoto's thyroiditis causes hypothyroidism (weight gain, constipation) and gritty eyes from associated autoimmune conditions like Sjögren's.

question: A 4-year-old boy presents with nose bleed. Child is well. On examination he has hemarthrosis.
explanation: Von Willebrand disease causes epistaxis and joint bleeding. Deficiency of vWF impairs platelet plug formation and factor VIII stabilization.

question: A 45-year-old man develops a cough only when he lies down. The cough improves when he sits up. His chest is clear.
explanation: GERD causes cough when lying down due to acid reflux. Lifestyle measures and proton pump inhibitors are first-line treatment.

question: A 65-year-old man with previous myocardial infarction develops cough and shortness of breath when he lies down in bed. The symptoms improve after getting out of bed and sitting up for 30 minutes.
explanation: Orthopnea suggests pulmonary edema from heart failure. Post-MI patients are at risk. Symptoms relieved by sitting up.

question: A 36-year-old woman with depression has been prescribed Selective Serotonin Re-uptake Inhibitor.
explanation: SSRIs don't require routine monitoring. ECG only if cardiac symptoms. Check sodium in high-risk patients for hyponatremia.

question: A 57-year-old man has been prescribed simvastatin for high cholesterol
explanation: Simvastatin requires LFTs before starting, within 3 months, then at 12 months. Monitor CK if muscle symptoms occur.

question: A 49-year-old woman with hypertension is prescribed ramipiril.
explanation: ACE inhibitors require renal function and electrolytes monitoring 1-2 weeks after starting, then monthly for 3 months, then every 6 months.

question: A 52-year-old man with back pain, dribbling nocturia, hematuria and weight loss
explanation: PSA is the tumor marker for prostate cancer. Symptoms include urinary issues, back pain and weight loss.

question: A 49-year-old woman with previous breast cancer treated with mastectomy and chemotherapy attends the clinic for follow up.
explanation: CA15-3 monitors breast cancer recurrence. Elevated levels may indicate metastasis. It's a prognostic marker.

question: A 62-year-old woman attends the clinic follow up. She has had hemicolectomy done 3 years ago for carcinoma of the caecum.
explanation: CEA monitors colorectal cancer surveillance after surgery. Elevated CEA may indicate recurrence.

question: A 72-year-old man is being treated for prostate cancer. Has developed gynecomastia
explanation: Bicalutamide is an anti-androgen causing gynecomastia by blocking testosterone receptors. Also causes hot flushes.

question: A 72-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer develops bruising over the lower abdomen. Full blood count, platelet count and clotting profile are all normal.
explanation: Steroids cause skin thinning and easy bruising even with normal labs. Common side effect of long-term use.

question: A 72-year-old man who is being treated for prostate cancer complains of hot flushes.
explanation: Goserelin is a GnRH agonist causing chemical castration. Hot flushes common due to testosterone suppression.

question: A 70-year-old woman presents with lower abdominal discomfort and bloating. Her mother had breast cancer. On examination she has an abdominal mass arising from the pelvic.
explanation: CA125 is the tumor marker for ovarian cancer. Symptoms include bloating and pelvic mass.

question: A 58-year-old man who has right upper quadrant pain, jaundice and de-arranged liver function tests.
explanation: AFP is elevated in hepatocellular carcinoma. RUQ pain with jaundice suggests liver pathology.

question: A 70-year-old woman presents with abdominal pain radiating to the back, weight loss and jaundice. She has Diabetes mellitus type 2.
explanation: CA19-9 is the tumor marker for pancreatic cancer. Abdominal pain radiating to back suggests pancreatic head tumor.

question: A 46-year-old woman has abdominal striae and central obesity. What is the SINGLE most appropriate treatment?
explanation: Cushing syndrome features include striae and obesity. Treatment includes enzyme inhibitors like ketoconazole, metyrapone or mitotane.

question: A 56-year-old woman develops painful and cold hands in winter.
explanation: Beta-blockers cause peripheral vasoconstriction and cold extremities. Can exacerbate Raynaud's phenomenon.

question: A 52-year-old man with hypertension has come for follow up. He complains of a dry cough.
explanation: Dry cough is classic side effect of ACE inhibitors like lisinopril. Caused by bradykinin accumulation.

question: A 58-year-old man with hypertension presents with recurrent dizziness. His standing blood pressure is 96/65 and lying blood pressure 117/77.
explanation: Thiazide diuretics cause postural hypotension. Elderly patients at higher risk. Monitor electrolytes.

question: A 61-year-old man with hypertension has come for follow up. He has developed bilateral ankle oedema.
explanation: Calcium channel blockers like amlodipine cause ankle swelling due to vasodilation. Common side effect.

question: A 9 weeks pregnant woman who has been admitted with morning sickness has developed spasm of the jaw and upward deviation of the eyes after being given a medication.
explanation: Metoclopramide causes acute dystonic reactions including oculogyric crisis. Common in young women. Treat with procyclidine.

question: A 33-year-old woman who is treated for vaginal discharge develops hot flushes following a wine testing party.
explanation: Metronidazole causes disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol. Symptoms include flushing, nausea, headache. Avoid alcohol during treatment.

question: A 35-year-old woman experiences pains and fingers turn blue when she is cold. On rewarming the fingers turn red.
explanation: Beta-blockers precipitate Raynaud's phenomenon. Cause vasospasm and cold extremities. Treat with calcium channel blockers.

question: A 50-year-old man collapsed at home. He is on peritoneal dialysis and his potassium is 2.1 mmol/L. He is known to have Long QT Syndrome.
explanation: Hypokalemia and long QT syndrome predispose to ventricular fibrillation. Life-threatening arrhythmia requires immediate defibrillation. torsades de point is also correct, both options.

question: A 61-year-old man develops palpitations 48 hours after being admitted with myocardial infarction. ECG shows broad complex tachycardia with a heart rate of 170 beats per minute.
explanation: Post-MI ventricular tachycardia is common. Broad complex tachycardia >150 bpm suggests VT. Requires urgent treatment.

question: A 51-year-old man presents with palpitations. ECG shows narrow complex tachycardia with a heart rate of 150 with 2:1 block
explanation: Atrial flutter shows sawtooth pattern with 2:1 block. Narrow complex regular tachycardia. Rate typically 150 bpm.

question: A 50-year-old man has had shortness of breath for 3 months. On examination he has no ascites, normal JVP, no peripheral oedema but he has fine bilateral basal crackles.
explanation: Fine bilateral basal crackles are classic for pulmonary fibrosis. Causes progressive dyspnea. HRCT shows honeycombing.

question: A 50-year-old man presents with 3 weeks history of shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain. On examination he has got bilateral crackles and a chest x-ray shows pleural effusion.
explanation: Pleuritic chest pain with pleural effusion suggests pneumonia. Acute onset with crackles. Heart failure doesn't cause pleuritic pain.
